text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; could you describe exactly where the pain is located and when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (symptomatically) secondary to prior trauma or inflammatory arthritis. The patient's history of falling 6 months ago and current symptoms (pain radiating to elbow, worsening with holding an infant) suggest possible post-traumatic deformity (e.g., malunion) or inflammatory arthritis affecting the wrist, potentially causing secondary nerve compression or mechanical restriction. Further imaging is required to confirm the underlying cause.
